key_concepts: ChatGPT can be used to sketch out scene graph layouts (e.g., which Containers and controls they should include) to provide wireframe-level guidance

content: When ChatGPT sketches out the scene graph layouts it uses notation which is not something Godot actually understands. A list of ChatGPT shorthand notation and their meanings are below:
c:# → means child spacing (the custom_constants/separation property of the HBoxContainer) is set to a specific number of px.
p:# → means padding or margin around the container is a specific number of px.
size_flags_h=# → means assigning a bit flag for how the UI element's parent nodes how they should resize and place the node on the X axis
size_flags_h=# → means assigning a bit flag for how the UI element's parent nodes how they should resize and place the node on the Y axis
Here’s a quick cheat sheet for Godot’s size flags bitmask values:
0 → SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER (default, minimal size, centered if extra space exists)
1 → FILL → Fill the space allocated, but don’t expand.
2 → EXPAND → Ask for extra space if available, but don’t necessarily fill it.
3 → EXPAND | FILL → Expand to take all extra space and fill it.
4 → SHRINK_BEGIN → Stick to the left side.
8 → SHRINK_END → Stick to the right side.
0 → default minimal size.
1 → FILL → Fill the vertical space given.
2 → EXPAND → Request extra vertical space.
3 → EXPAND | FILL → Expand vertically and fill the space.
4 → SHRINK_BEGIN → Stick to the top.
8 → SHRINK_END → Stick to the bottom.
In the Godot Editor, select the UI element and in the Inspector expand [k]Control > Layout > Container Sizing[/k] (Image 1). To set the specific size flags, use the following settings:

image.caption: Image 1 - Where to adjust the size flags in the Godot Editor

content: To set the specific size flags, use the following settings:
0 → Shrink Begin
1 → Fill
2 → set manually in raw .tscn file
3 → set manually in raw .tscn file
4 → Shrink Center
8 → Shrink End
